newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss govt seeks cantons' support for growth pact.
newsitem.headline: Swiss govt seeks cantons' support for growth pact.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet will launch a 550 million Swiss franc economic stimulus package if it can persuade cantonal and local governments to boost their own outlays on infrastructure, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.

"The investment programme under discussion aims to stimulate the economy and employment," it said, adding 550 million francs in federal funds could trigger overall spending of 1.8 billion for the recession-bound economy that has stagnated since 1990.

"But the effectiveness of the measures depends on the willingness of cantons and local governments to provide additional funds on their part," it added, noting talks would take place in late January and early February.
An agreed programme could be put to parliament in April.
A ministry spokesman said the federal government would not proceed on its own if cash-strapped lower governments opted not to take part in the programme.

Parliament agreed last month to earmark funds for a stimulus package to be held in reserve in the 1997 federal budget, which projects a deficit of 5.77 billion francs. The 1996 deficit is budgeted at 4.05 billion, but could be up to one billion higher.

The 1997 budget is based on projected GDP growth of 1.5 percent, well above most analysts' forecasts that the economy will be flat to up 0.5 percent. GDP is expected to have shrunk around 0.6 percent in 1996. GDP rose 0.1 percent in 1995.
